reader.requirement: At --std 85, when a level-01 File/Working-Storage entry carries both REDEFINES and GLOBAL, only that entry (the subject) and its subordinates are global names visible in contained programs; the redefined object (and its subordinates) is not global unless it carries GLOBAL itself, and conversely a GLOBAL object does not make an un-GLOBAL redefiner global.

reader.notes: Global-name registration takes exactly the entries whose GLOBAL clause was admitted, so the REDEFINES object never becomes global through its redefiner; the Tier-A bridge reuses the canonical's storage member without exposing its name. Both refusal directions and the positive group form behave as the 1985 text says.
